title: Mathematics Genealogy Project: infrastructure model for formal advisor-lineage records
summary: The Mathematics Genealogy Project is promoted as the first genealogy-lane record, but as an infrastructure model rather than as a full imported database. It demonstrates a durable, queryable way to encode formal doctoral advisor/student relationships while also exposing the project-level caveats this cube must carry: community submissions, manual review, incomplete recent years, and unequal coverage.

status_history.note: The seed document named the Mathematics Genealogy Project as a gold-standard starting point for genealogy infrastructure.
Promoted using MGP, NDSU, and AMS institutional sources; no individual genealogy edges imported yet.

Coverage and recency caveats are treated as substantive record fields, not footnotes.

confidence_ladder.condition: formal degree/advisor relation appears in MGP and can be verified from university or dissertation source
MGP entry exists but underlying university/dissertation evidence not independently checked in this cube

scope_cautions: Formal doctoral advisor relation is not the same as influence, collaboration, mentorship, reading, reaction, or transmission.
Recent years may have gaps and country coverage varies, per MGP FAQ.
This cube should import edges only after source/permanence rules are set.
type_payload.why_it_matters_for_missing_half: It supplies a mature model for the genealogy half of the project: record the relation type, source, uncertainty, and completeness caveat rather than treating intellectual ancestry as folklore.

links.note: Dartmouth-style scene records need stricter relation labels than formal advisor trees.

handling_notes: Genealogy can erase informal, undercredited, non-Western, and non-doctoral transmission; this record must not become a prestige-only filter.
Avoid contact or personal-data claims for living people unless sources and purpose justify them.
